growing up in Hong Kong in a very traditional Chinese family, being gay just wasn’t an option. As a kid, I knew deep down that I liked girls. But my family was so conservative, and I loved them. I held out hope that maybe I just hadn’t met the right guy yet. I didn’t want to disappoint everyone. in college in the US, I realized that was never going to happen. I’m 100% a lesbian🤪 And that’s when I met Madi! we grew up so differently- her in Houston TX, me in Hong Kong. We were worlds apart. Madi grew up VERY southern and basically lived off a diet of chicken tenders and Mac & cheese. So it was extra meaningful that she was always trying to learn more about where I came from. At dim sum, she would be down to try everything🥺🥺 she even went out of her way to look up the dates and meanings of Chinese holidays. One day, I came over to her apartment on Chinese new year (I had totally forgotten it had started) and she had set up some flowers for me and even written a note in Chinese inside a red packet😭😭 (I told her afterwards that u don’t rly give red packets to your peers but it’s the thought that counts) I’ll never forget when she brought me to the rodeo in Houston and I met her family. Even though they were catholic and were nervous about meeting me, they welcomed me with open arms. Now, they invite me over for every family occasion. Madi’s mom even made me my own personalized stocking for Christmas 🥹 Finally, I decided to take madi home to meet my family in Hong Kong. I had never brought anyone home before😳 But before long, I realized I had nothing to be nervous about. My dad (as a typical Chinese man does) tried to outdrink madi at dinner, but his lightweight ass could NOT compete. He was automatically impressed by her 😏 Madi played arcade games with my brother and went kayaking with my sister. She vibed with everyone🥹 Now, we’ve been married for over a year and a half, and it’s been the best year of my life. Our home truly combines the best parts of how we grew up. We see her family every Christmas, and see my family in Hong Kong every summer. Shoutout to summer break for teachers🤪🤪 We celebrate Chinese holidays like mid-autumn festival, and I sometimes go to mass with her at our local church (shoutout to Catholic Lesbians group at St Francis Xavier in NYC🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍🌈)! Our diet is a mix of collard greens, stir-fried Chinese vegetables, seafood boils, and congee. If only little me could see our life together. I know she would be proud🥰

A Quiet Life, an Extraordinary Legacy 📷 Du Yingrong and Lu Suying lived a remarkably simple life in China. The childless couple carefully saved money and were known for sharing inexpensive meals costing only a few dollars. But behind their modest lifestyle was an extraordinary act of kindness. After learning about children suffering from congenital heart disease, the couple donated 5 million yuan—around $735,000—to help fund lifesaving treatment. Their generosity eventually helped 455 children receive the medical care they desperately needed. They never lived extravagantly or sought attention for what they had done. Instead, they chose to use their savings to give vulnerable children a healthier future. Their beautiful story proves that true wealth isn’t measured by what we keep, but by how many lives we touch. 📷 See less
